inputs.original_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s call for a political resolution matters, but it rings hollow alongside talk of Israel’s “unwavering stance” and a continuing operation. Security built around military pressure risks deepening the conditions that make people across the region unsafe. A real resolution must address the structures driving the conflict and uphold everyone’s rights—not normalize endless escalation as the only path forward.
inputs.modified_text: Daniel Rubenstein is right that this needs a political resolution, but calls for one mean little when Israel pairs them with an “unwavering stance” and a continuing operation. Military pressure does not create lasting safety; it entrenches a system where those with the least power bear the greatest cost. Any real resolution must confront the structural inequality driving the conflict and protect Palestinians’ rights and security alongside everyone else’s. Endless escalation is not peace.
